self_assessment: Topics.validateTags now takes an optional tid (defaulting to null) and loads the topic's current tags when one is given, so creates see an empty currentTags and edits see the real list. It derives addedTags and removedTags by diffing the submitted list against currentTags and, for non-privileged users, rejects adding any tag in meta.config.systemTags with [[error:cant-use-system-tag]] and removing any with the new [[error:cant-remove-system-tag]]; privileged users are exempt from both, and the category minTags/maxTags checks run first and are untouched. posts/edit.js passes the topic's tid through, which is what fixes the reported bug - a regular user editing a topic no longer drops a moderator-added system tag - while topics/create.js and posts/queue.js stay on the create path. Added SocketTopics.canRemoveTag(socket, data), which throws [[error:invalid-data]] without data.tag and otherwise returns isPrivileged || !systemTags.includes(data.tag), and added the cant-remove-system-tag key to public/language/en-GB/error.json. Verified by extracting the two new function bodies straight out of the modified sources and running them against stubbed meta/user/categories/Topics: keeping or reordering a system tag on edit passes, dropping one is rejected, adding one is rejected on both create and edit, privileged users can do both, min/max limits and the invalid-data guard still behave, and canRemoveTag returns the right booleans and throws on bad input. NodeBB's own suite needs a live redis/mongo plus a built asset bundle, so it could not be run; node --check passes on all three changed JS files and the error.json still parses.
